decisions.decision: Rob Bowen was reappointed deputy moderator for the year, with no objection raised, rather than by formal vote.
The moderator, on advice of town counsel, ruled that town meeting could vote only the total dollar figure of the Article 6 capital plan and could not amend or debate individual line items within it.
The finance committee agreed among itself to undertake a deeper review of the capital planning process during the coming year.

The superintendent indicated that if the primary school AC project needs a modest additional amount, the district would seek to cover it within its operating budget, but a larger shortfall would come back to town meeting via a future capital request.
The moderator, after conferring with town counsel, voided the initial vote on the Bertram Article 19 amendment because it had not been properly worded, and had the amendment re-read and re-voted.
The moderator ruled Carl Strathmeyer's proposed amendment to Article 27 (restricting where a Zone One could be created) out of scope of the article as warranted, and disallowed debate on it.

minutes.headline: Town Meeting passed the FY23 town/school budget and capital plan, and cut back old primary school park funding by floor amendment.
minutes.summary: This was Lunenburg's annual Town Meeting, working through a full warrant covering the FY23 town and school operating budget, the capital plan, a new facilities director position, and numerous bylaw and building articles including the Woodruff property cleanup, old primary school demolition, sewer bylaw waivers, a marijuana licensing fix, and the water supply protection district. Nearly every article passed, though residents amended the old primary school demolition article down from its original funding level after a lengthy, twice-redone floor debate, and repeatedly pushed back on whether the capital plan should have allowed item-by-item votes. The meeting also passed over a citizen petition to expand the sewer service area and took up a resolution supporting a new state flag, with the final tallies on the water-district and flag articles not clearly captured.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting passed the FY23 town and school operating budget as one omnibus article, funded without drawing on free cash or stabilization.
The FY23 capital plan passed as a single up-or-down total after the moderator ruled, on town counsel's advice, that individual projects could not be voted or amended separately.
After a floor debate redone once for a procedural flaw, voters cut back the old primary school article to cover demolition and design only, not the fuller park funding first proposed.
A new facilities director position was created, and free cash was approved to clean up illegally dumped waste on the town-owned Woodruff property.
Votes on the water supply protection district bylaw and a resolution on the state flag were not clearly captured on the recording.

why_it_matters: The operating budget vote sets what residents' tax bill funds for town and school services in FY23, including new police, fire and school staff positions described by the town manager and superintendent.

Because the capital plan can only be voted as one total, residents cannot currently approve or reject individual projects like the senior center HVAC or the primary school classroom AC separately — a process several people at the meeting pushed back on.
The old primary school site now has money for demolition and design, but not for a built-out park, so what that land becomes is still an open question for a future town meeting or town decision.
watch_next: Whether the primary school AC project comes back to a future town meeting as a capital request if it exceeds what the school's operating budget can absorb.
A future decision on the final design or use — park versus open space — of the old primary school lot.
